newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals seen opening lower.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals seen opening lower.

text.p: COMEX and NYMEX precious metals futures were called to open weaker on Wednesday as gold braced itself following a report saying central banks might sell gold to raise money.
COMEX June was gold was seen opening down $0.50 to $1.00 an ounce from Tuesday's close. Bullion was quoted at $340.65/$340.95.
In London gold was fixed at $340.70 Wednesday morning compared with $341.60 on Tuesday afternoon.
COMEX May silver was called to open 1.00 to 2.00 cents an ounce lower.
Andy Smith of UBS said central banks were likely to consider several ways of activating their gold reserves, but not all would harm the price.
But markets were right to fear gold sales by European cenral banks to qualify for inclusion in the single currency, Smith added in a report.
Smith's comments added fuel to bearish sentiment, traders said.
COMEX warehouse gold stocks slipped 55,844 ounces to 943,151 ounces Tuesday.
COMEX silver stocks were down 786,441 ounces Tuesday to 189,086,531 ounces.
NYMEX July platinum and NYMEX June palladium were called to open $0.50 to $1.00 an ounce weaker.
Platinum also developed some weakness overnight with follow through selling from New York's losses on Tuesday, despite continuing delays in Russian metal deliveries to Japan.
